raw.cause: logger serves a channel made with ChannelCreate(_NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY), so its receiving thread keeps its own low priority instead of inheriting the client's. While nav, running at the priority it inherited from display, sits REPLY-blocked in MsgSend, the priority-20 media job preempts logger's 2 ms of formatting. A normal ~2 ms reply then stretches to ~50 ms, which is one full 45 ms media burst plus the work itself.
raw.qnx_call: ChannelCreate with _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY in logger (run_logger); nav's MsgSend to logger is held REPLY-blocked behind it
raw.fix_summary: Remove _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY from the logger channel so logger's MsgReceive inherits the waiting client's priority and media can no longer preempt it while nav waits. The same effect comes from running with COCKPIT_FIXED=1, or from having logger always use serve()/name_attach. If logging must truly stay low priority, change the contract instead: have clients log asynchronously, for example with MsgSendPulse or a queue thread, rather than blocking on a synchronous MsgSend.
